items.criterion: Deliverable is provided as a single Excel workbook file (.xlsx).
items.evidence: Local_Musician_Weekly_Payroll.xlsx

items.criterion: Workbook includes a dedicated Rates table that centralizes all contract rates and amounts (no hard-coded numbers embedded in pay formulas).
items.evidence: Setup!C21:C25 and Payroll!I8:T8 reference centralized rate parameters.

items.criterion: Workbook includes a Roster area that captures a unique musician identifier, musician name, and instrument/role for each musician, and uses the unique identifier to link assignments and summaries.
items.evidence: Roster!C6 captures an ID, but Schedule and Payroll link by fixed roster row, not unique identifier.

items.criterion: Workbook includes a Schedule area that records, for each service, the date, service type, and either start/end time or duration, and provides a method to assign musicians to each service.
items.evidence: Schedule!B7:G7 records service details; N8:AQ47 provides attendance assignments.

items.criterion: Workbook includes a Per‑Person Summary that shows pay by category per musician (at minimum: audit, sound check, rehearsal, performance, premium, doubling, vacation) and the per‑musician total.
items.evidence: Payroll!I7:U7 includes all required categories and gross pay.

items.criterion: Workbook includes a Weekly Payroll summary that aggregates each musician’s weekly totals across all categories and lists one row per musician for submission.
items.evidence: Payroll!A8:U15 shows one linked summary row per musician.

items.criterion: Workbook includes an Instructions or Notes section that explains required inputs, where to update rates, and which cells are protected or calculated.
items.evidence: Instructions!C5:C9, C12, and C17 explain inputs, calculated cells, and rate updates.

items.criterion: Roster provides a data entry field for musician name.
items.evidence: Roster!B6='Musician Name'

items.criterion: Roster provides a data entry field for the primary instrument/role for each musician.
items.evidence: Roster!D6='Primary Instrument'

items.criterion: Schedule or input area provides a data entry field for the number of audits per musician (or assigns musicians to audit services) that feeds audit pay.
items.evidence: Schedule!N10:N11='A'; Payroll!H8 counts assigned audits.

items.criterion: Schedule or input area provides data entry for the number of 1‑hour sound checks per musician (or explicit assignment to 1‑hour sound check services).
items.evidence: Schedule!D9, F9:G9, N9:W9 assign musicians to a one-hour sound check.

items.criterion: Schedule or input area provides data entry for the number of 2‑hour sound checks per musician (or explicit assignment to 2‑hour sound check services).
items.evidence: Schedule!F7:G7 accepts sound-check times; K8 selects Rate_SC2 for two-hour calls.

items.criterion: Schedule or input area provides a data entry field for the number of rehearsals per musician or total rehearsal hours that feed rehearsal pay per the CBA unit.
items.evidence: Schedule!J8 calculates paid rehearsal hours; Payroll!F8 and J8 aggregate assigned rehearsals.

items.criterion: Schedule or input area provides a data entry field for the number of performances per musician that feeds performance pay.
items.evidence: Payroll!E8 counts Performance services marked X.

items.criterion: Rates table includes an input for the per‑service base wage for performances used by the model.
items.evidence: Setup!C21 looks up RT_Base; Instructions!C17 identifies editable base-wage rate rows.

items.criterion: Rates table includes an input for the per‑audit rate used by the model.
items.evidence: Instructions!C25 specifies base wage per audit; Payroll!L8 uses Rate_Base.

items.criterion: Rates table includes an input for the weekly guarantee rate (if present in the CBA excerpt) used by the model.
items.evidence: Setup!C22 looks up RT_Guar.

items.criterion: Rates table includes an input for the per‑hour rehearsal rate (or per‑service rehearsal rate, matching the CBA unit) used by the model.
items.evidence: Setup!C23 looks up RT_Reh.

items.criterion: Rates table includes inputs for both 1‑hour and 2‑hour sound check rates used by the model.
items.evidence: Setup!C24:C25 look up RT_SC1 and RT_SC2.

items.criterion: Roster includes a field indicating whether a synthesizer player is a regular or substitute musician, and the model uses this status if the CBA sets different terms.
items.evidence: Roster!E7 and R7 distinguish synth substitutes; Payroll!I8 applies different payment logic.

items.criterion: Roster or eligibility inputs include checkboxes/fields for trumpet players to qualify for either a 20% or 15% premium per Section 2(a) of the CBA excerpt, applied by the model at the correct rate.
items.evidence: Roster!F14 and T14 select lead-chair versus standard trumpet premium.

items.criterion: Roster or eligibility inputs include checkboxes/fields for French horn players to qualify for either a 20% or 15% premium per Section 2(a) of the CBA excerpt, applied by the model at the correct rate.
items.evidence: Roster!T16 applies Prem_Lead for designated horn only when ShowHasTrumpet='N'.

items.criterion: Roster or eligibility inputs include checkboxes/fields for violinists to qualify for either a 20% or 15% premium per Section 2(b) of the CBA excerpt, applied by the model at the correct rate.
items.evidence: Roster!F8 and T8 distinguish violin lead-chair and standard premiums.

items.criterion: Roster or eligibility inputs include a field indicating whether a musician qualifies for the premium defined in Section 2(c) of the CBA excerpt, applied by the model at the correct rate.
items.evidence: Roster!F9, F15, and T9:T15 designate standard first-local premiums.

items.criterion: Roster or inputs include a field for the number of instruments a musician plays to drive the doubling premium calculation per Section 4 of the CBA excerpt.
items.evidence: Roster!H6:L6 lists doubles; S7 counts them and W7 calculates the percentage.

items.criterion: Service type entries are constrained to a controlled list that maps to the CBA categories (e.g., Performance, Rehearsal, 1‑hour Sound Check, 2‑hour Sound Check, Audit) to prevent invalid types.
items.evidence: Visible Schedule formulas accept arbitrary nonblank types as performances; controlled-list validation is not shown in the truncated extraction.

items.criterion: Rate application logic selects rates automatically based on the service date (by choosing the most recent effective date not after the service) or a contract‑year selector; per‑row manual rate typing is not required.
items.evidence: Instructions!C34: 'rates ... in effect on the week ending date'; service-date changes only receive warnings.

items.criterion: The model calculates performance pay per musician using the Rates table and the number of performance services assigned.
items.evidence: Payroll!I8 calculates performance wages from E8, Rate_Base, and Rate_Guar.

items.criterion: The model calculates rehearsal pay per musician using the CBA‑defined unit (per hour or per service) and the recorded quantity for each musician.
items.evidence: Schedule!K8=ROUND(J8*Rate_Reh,2); Payroll!J8 sums assigned rehearsal pay.

items.criterion: The model calculates sound check pay per musician with separate treatment for 1‑hour and 2‑hour sound checks at their respective rates.
items.evidence: Schedule!K8 selects Rate_SC1 or Rate_SC2; Payroll!K8 aggregates assigned sound checks.

items.criterion: The model calculates audit pay per musician using the audit rate from the Rates table and the number of audits performed.
items.evidence: Payroll!H8 counts eligible audits; L8=ROUND(H8*Rate_Base,2).

items.criterion: The model calculates position/instrument premiums at the CBA‑specified percentage(s) and applies them to the correct base wages for eligible musicians per Sections 2(a), 2(b), and 2(c).
items.evidence: Roster!T7 selects Prem_Lead/Prem_Std; Payroll!N8 applies the selected rate to scale wages.

items.criterion: The model calculates doubling premiums per Section 4 using the correct tier thresholds and bases, supporting multiple doubles where applicable.
items.evidence: Payroll!R8 uses M8 excluding position premiums; final message explicitly says premiums and doubling are not compounded.

items.criterion: The model calculates vacation pay at the CBA‑specified percentage or flat amount based on the eligible wage categories.
items.evidence: Payroll!T8=ROUND(S8*Vac_Pct,2); Instructions!C27 specifies 5.5% of total earnings.

items.criterion: The model calculates a total pay per musician that sums audit, sound check, rehearsal, performance, premium, doubling, and vacation pay.
items.evidence: Payroll!S8 sums wages, audits, premiums, doubling; U8 adds vacation.

items.criterion: Per‑Person Summary totals reconcile exactly to the Weekly Payroll summary totals when summed across all musicians.
items.evidence: Payroll provides both per-person and weekly summaries; Setup!C53 links its grand total to Payroll!U38.

items.criterion: The model flags a rehearsal entry if the total rehearsal hours per day for any musician are less than 3 hours or greater than 5 hours.
items.evidence: Schedule!BS8 tests consecutive call hours, not per-musician daily totals; BZ8 only notes minimum-call adjustments.

items.criterion: The model flags a rehearsal if its end time is after 6:30 p.m.
items.evidence: Schedule!BQ8 tests rehearsal end against Reh_Day_End and feeds VIOLATION status.

items.criterion: The model flags a rehearsal if its end time is before 9:00 a.m.
items.evidence: Schedule!BO8 tests start time, not end time before 9:00 a.m.

items.criterion: The model flags when a schedule entry’s service type does not have a corresponding rate in the Rates table for the relevant effective date/contract year.
items.evidence: Setup!C36 checks period coverage only; Schedule!K8 defaults unrecognized types to Rate_Base without a missing-category-rate check.

items.criterion: Workbook input cells are visually distinguishable from calculated cells via consistent formatting.
items.evidence: Instructions!B11:C12 identifies yellow/blue inputs and grey calculated cells.

items.criterion: Workbook contains no external links and requires no macros to function.
items.evidence: Visible formulas use internal worksheet references and standard Excel functions; deliverable is .xlsx.
